bullets.text: LME aluminium $3,039/t, down 2.6% on the week; Emkay sees lower prices weighing on Hindalco and NALCO, VAML and Vedanta offsetting.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals Weekly: Aluminium hovering at base case $3,000-3,100/t

detail.summary: Supply has eased: EGA's Al Taweelah restarted, China's August output hit a record 3.9mt, Indonesia added capacity and a stronger dollar weighed on sentiment. Non-ferrous earnings sit in line with Emkay's base case and spot upside is small, while ferrous has 10-20% upside; Emkay still favours VAML and Hindalco on the aluminium cycle.
points: $3,039/t aluminium, -2.6% w/w; base case $3,000-3,100/t
China Aug-26 output record 3.9mt; exports 516kt CY26YTD vs 582kt
Spot EBITDA upside: VAML ~1%, NALCO ~7%, HNDL balanced (hedges)
Non-ferrous 4.4-5.6x FY28E EV/EBITDA vs ferrous 5.5-7.5x
Metals stocks -3-7% on the week; prefers VAML, HNDL

bullets.text: CLSA 2Q metals preview: softer quarter on lower prices and input costs; Hindalco hit at India level; steel near term, aluminium longer term.
bullets.source: CLSA sales — NVIDIA @ VIZAG | Metals Preview | O&G Preview

detail.summary: Sales gist of CLSA's 2Q preview: a soft September quarter from lower prices and higher input costs, but flat and long steel prices have risen since quarter-end, which should carry 2H. Hindalco takes the impact in its India business; the house prefers steel near term and aluminium on a longer horizon.
points: Softer 2Q: lower prices, higher input costs
Flat and long prices up after the Sept quarter; supports 2H
Hindalco impacted at India business level
Preference: steel near term, aluminium longer term

bullets.text: Domestic steel prices at a 53-month high; Elara sees spot spreads widening since June, pointing to Q3FY27 margin expansion, flats over longs.
bullets.source: Elara — Metals & Mining: Spot steel spreads continue to widen (monthly)

detail.summary: Q2 is seasonally weak (HRC averages -5.7% over five years) but firm HRC in Q2FY27 favours flat producers while rebar and semis corrected from Q1. Tight mill and distributor inventory, shutdowns and input costs keep spreads firm, and H1 consumption outgrew domestic production despite a 24% rise in imports.

bullets.text: Emkay: HRC Rs64,000/t and rebar Rs63,900/t, up 10.5% and 30% over the quarter; JSTL and Tata outperform, JINDALST and SAIL lag.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals Weekly: Aluminium hovering at base case $3,000-3,100/t

detail.summary: Emkay's spot scenario shows ferrous strengthening on a raw-material-cost-led and demand-driven recovery in HRC and rebar, even as 2QFY27 ferrous margins stay under pressure from weaker realisations and coking coal. At spot, FY27E ferrous EBITDA carries 10-20% upside to base case; JSTL and JINDALST remain the preferred names.

bullets.text: Oct dealer checks: West (ex-Mumbai) +Rs5-20/bag, North +Rs5-10/bag, South up again on top of September; East demand weak.
bullets.source: JPM — Concrete Insights: October: Pricing improvements; ahead of schedule

detail.summary: JPM's 12-dealer October check finds prices up in most regions, extending September's momentum. North demand is running ahead of expectations on pre-winter construction; East stays weak on labour shortages. Pricing momentum through Nov/Dec is what defends margins.
points: 12 dealers surveyed across India
West ex-Mumbai +Rs5-20/bag; one dealer saw earlier hikes rolled back
North +Rs5-10/bag; demand pulled forward ahead of winter construction curbs
South up further after September hikes; demand mediocre until post-Diwali
Construction lending +25% YoY in August; central capex slowing

bullets.text: JPM sees risk of negative Sep-qtr surprises as costs outlast guidance of Rs80-140/MT increases, smaller players worse; UTCEM remains top pick.
bullets.source: JPM — Concrete Insights: October: Pricing improvements; ahead of schedule

detail.summary: Coal/petcoke, gypsum, power, packaging and a weaker USDINR have pressured costs for longer than expected, flowing into the Dec and Mar quarters. JPM thinks the downside risk is to the guided Rs80-140/MT increase, with larger companies managing better. It prefers UTCEM for defending volumes and margins.

Bias: larger companies manage costs better than smaller ones
Post-Diwali price hikes key to offsetting costs
UTCEM top pick in sector

bullets.text: Accenture guides mid-single-digit growth FY27-28, mid-high single digit only by FY29 via acquired businesses; Kotak reads stagnant growth for Indian incumbents.
bullets.source: Kotak — IT Services - Accenture: Growth acceleration driven by M&A-aided new opportunities

detail.summary: Accenture's investor day sets growth at mid-single digits through FY28, accelerating to mid-high single digits in FY29 on the acquired network of businesses (6% of revenue, to double). Kotak's read-through: the guide limits downside from AI deflation for Indian incumbents but implies stagnant growth, and acceleration needs participation in new TAM.
points: Core (94% of revenue) grows mid-single digits to FY29
Acquired businesses 6% of revenue, to double by FY29
Margin +10-30bps a year for 3 years; FCF 110%+ of net income
TAM US$3tn vs US$1.5tn: US$700bn core AI, US$800bn new markets
Inorganic growth ~2% a year; 18k AI projects in FY26

bullets.text: Tata Elxsi 2Q beat (revenue +2.3% QoQ, EBIT margin 19.7%): Kotak keeps SELL, FV Rs3,200 from 3,000; Avendus upgrades to ADD.
bullets.source: Kotak — Tata Elxsi (CMP Rs3,426, FV Rs3,200, SELL): An improved quarter (+8 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Broad-based growth across media, healthcare and transport with margins helped by currency (60-70bps) and utilisation up to 78%. Kotak raises EPS 2-3% but stays SELL at 25x FY28E: growth has been volatile, Europe auto is weak, JLR is 24% of revenue, and 1.8% CQGR is needed in 2H for high-single-digit growth.

Higher WPI lifts nominal GDP but raises retail-inflation upside risk and the pressure to pass input costs through.
